hero.title: Home base for China's furry fans
hero.lead: FuzzStar is an organization built by and for furry culture enthusiasts in China. We shoot videos, cut edits, run events — and keep a comfortable space where everyone can just be.

directions.title: What we do
directions.lead: The org does a bit of everything — if it sounds fun, you're welcome:

items.title: Video creation
items.text: From picking topics to shooting and cutting, there's always someone to team up with — originals or fan edits. Need a storyboard buddy or a color grader? Shout in the chat.

items.title: Community life
items.text: Show off your OC, talk fursuits, plan meetups. Few rules, one clear bottom line: respect each other, don't start fights.

items.title: Group projects
items.text: Collab videos, cross-community events, offline meetups — if enough people are in, any idea becomes a project. Bring the idea; we'll bring the hands.

ctaBand.title: Come hang out first
ctaBand.text: Website copy is just words — the people in the chat are the real thing. Pick QQ or Discord and say hi.

hero.title: About FuzzStar
hero.lead: Where we came from, what we keep busy with, and how we treat each other.

origin.title: How it started
paragraphs: FuzzStar began as a tiny group chat. We were all into furry culture and couldn't sit still — someone wanted to shoot videos, someone wanted to edit, someone just wanted people to talk to. So we ended up together.
The group kept growing until the little chat became what it is today. We don't have any grand plans — we just think furry fans in China deserve a steady, comfortable place to land.

items.title: Content creation
items.text: Videos, write-ups, fan works — the org divides up the work, and group members are free to start their own projects. Need a hand? Just ask.

items.title: Running the community
items.text: Two community groups, kept alive by everyone: mods hold the line, group members help each other out.

items.title: Events
items.text: Online watch-alongs, group shoots, con meetups — big or small, if someone wants to organize it, someone else will help.

items.title: Collaborations
items.text: We're always open to working with other creators and groups. Reach us via email or the community chat.

values.title: How we get along
items: Art and OCs belong to their creators: ask before reposting, adapting, or crediting.
Talk things out. Criticize the work, never the person.
Newcomers not knowing the rules is normal — guide first, punish later.
Keep private things private: no digging up identities or sharing chats without permission.

outlook.title: What's next
outlook.text: Keep the community solid so newcomers don't get lost; back group members' creative work and pitch in where we can; team up more with others and grow the scene a little.

hero.title: Join us
hero.lead: One click puts you in a community group. Joining the org as staff takes an application — both are on this page.

steps.title: Three steps to join the org

items.title: Join a community first
items.text: Pick QQ or Discord and click through — you're a member of that group.

items.title: Talk to the mod team
items.text: Once inside, tell the mod team you'd like to apply to the org.

items.title: Pass the review
items.text: Follow their instructions to submit your info. Once approved, you're staff.

requirements.title: Before you apply to the org
items: You agree with the charter and will follow the community rules.
You respect other people's art, OCs, and privacy.
You treat yourself as part of the community — speak up when something's off.

items.q: Is joining the group the same as joining the org?
items.a: No. Joining a group just makes you a member of that group — hang out however you like. Joining the org means applying to become staff: a review, and real responsibilities.
QQ is easier for everyday use in China; Discord works better abroad or if you prefer English. Both are welcome.
The review checks whether you're on board with the charter and willing to follow the rules. If you don't pass, ask the mods why — you can always reapply.

hero.title: Organization charter
hero.lead: How FuzzStar runs, who counts as a group member and who counts as staff, and what rights and duties come with it.

draft.title: This is a draft
draft.description: The wording is still being polished; the mod team's final version takes precedence. Feedback is welcome in the community chat.

articles.text: The organization is named FuzzStar: a volunteer, non-profit interest group made up primarily of furry culture enthusiasts in China.
Its mission is to bring furry culture fans together, encourage creative exchange and content production, and provide group members and staff with a friendly, stable community environment.
The organization is not for profit, must not be used for any illegal activity, and must not be used to seek improper benefit for any individual.

This charter is an internal agreement that defines member status, departmental duties, and standards of conduct. It creates no rights or obligations under the law; where laws apply, those laws prevail.
Joining a community group makes you a member of that group. Members of those groups who agree with this charter and are willing to follow the community rules may apply to become staff (org members).
How to join the org: group members apply to the mod team, submit what the mod team asks for, and become staff once the review is approved.

Staff are organized into three parallel departments — Creators, Development, and Community — with the duties set out in Chapter III. The mod team is the executive body, drawn from staff and confirmed by the mod team.
Withdrawal: anyone may leave a community group at any time. Staff may resign by giving the mod team notice and handing over their duties. Resigning does not affect their standing as a group member.
Mod team duties: day-to-day operations, external contact, keeping and publishing the accounts, enforcing this charter, and carrying out discipline.
Creators department duties: content creation, including video, written work and fan works, plus producing content for events.
Development department duties: maintaining the website and tooling, technical support, and asset and data management.
Community department duties: day-to-day group operations, organizing and running events, member reception, and onboarding newcomers.
Each department works independently within its remit. Matters that cross departments, or that affect staff as a whole, are discussed and decided by the mod team.
The right to take part in departmental work, events, and projects, and to use the resources the group provides.
The right to share opinions and suggestions about the group's work and to join discussions that affect it.
The right to know about the group's affairs and the published record of income and spending.
The right to appeal any decision that concerns oneself.
Staff retain authorship and copyright over their own works and OCs; others may not repost or use them without permission.
Follow this charter and all rules of the community groups.
Respect other members: no personal attacks, no flame wars, no harassment.
Respect others' creations and copyrights; do not repost, misuse, or republish without the original author's permission.
Protect personal privacy: do not dig up identities, do not share other people's personal information, chat logs, or images, and do not publish someone else's likeness without their consent.
Help maintain community order and report rule-breaking behavior to the mod team in a timely manner.
Do not engage in illegal activity or private profit in the organization's name.
Staff must also carry out their departmental duties, cooperate with the mod team, and not use their position for private gain.
Funding comes mainly from voluntary donations, used for events, tooling, and operating costs.
Donations are voluntary: nobody may pressure others to give, apportion a share, or demand money in the group's name.
Earmarked use: donated funds are spent on the agreed purpose and may not be diverted.
Open accounts: the mod team assigns a member to record income and spending, and this is published in the community after each event.
Non-profit: nobody may take a share, commission, or profit from group funds in the group's name.
For group members: depending on severity, a warning, limits on posting or other community privileges, or removal from the group.
For staff: depending on severity, a warning, suspension of departmental duties or privileges, or revocation of staff status.
Revoking staff status requires agreement from more than half of the mod team, and the reasons must be given to the person in writing.
Anyone disciplined may appeal to the mod team within seven days of being notified; the mod team must respond within seven days. One further review may be requested.
Anyone using the group's name for illegal activity or private profit loses all authorization and their staff status.
The mod team interprets this charter and publishes the interpretation to the community.
Amendments must be discussed and passed by the mod team, and take effect after being announced to the community.
This charter takes effect once the mod team ratifies it. Draft version v0.9, revised 26 September 2026.
